# Shot list & Veo prompts (Flow/Veo, generated by you)

Continuity (paste before every prompt):

**Athlete (use in EVERY shot):** one man, about 25 years old, athletic build, short dark hair, light stubble, plain navy training T-shirt, black shorts, plain white trainers. No logos, no text, no numbers on clothing.
**Physiotherapist (use in every clinical shot):** one woman, about 35, hair tied back, plain white short-sleeve clinical top, no name badge, no logos, calm professional manner.
**Global rules for every prompt:** photorealistic, natural skin, real human proportions and joint mechanics, cinematic lighting, 9:16 vertical, 8 seconds, no on-screen text, no watermark, no brand logos, no extra people unless stated, no exaggerated injury, no visibly impossible joint angle.

## A1 opening (6.5 s of 8)
Wide-to-medium tracking shot of the athlete sprinting on a floodlit football pitch at dusk. He plants his right foot, the ankle rolls inward slightly, he slows to a walk and bends slightly toward the ankle with a pained expression. Final 2 s: camera pushes in towards the right ankle. Cinematic, shallow depth of field.

## A2 football ankle
Medium shot: the athlete, in football kit-style plain shirt, lands from a jump on a football pitch, the right foot turns inward, he stops and lifts the foot off the ground. Natural, not exaggerated.

## A3 hamstring
Side tracking shot: the athlete is running, slows down, and reaches toward the back of his right thigh with one hand, grimacing mildly, walking it off.

## A4 knee
Medium shot: the athlete sits on the edge of a pitch bench and indicates discomfort around the right knee with one hand, looking down at it.

## B1 assessment
Bright physiotherapy clinic. The athlete sits on a treatment table with his right lower leg exposed. The physiotherapist sits facing the ankle, looks at it carefully, gently feels around the ankle, then gently moves the foot through a small comfortable range while speaking with him. No forceful manipulation. Camera: slow medium shot, side-front angle.

## B2 mobility start
Same clinic, same two people. The athlete sits on the treatment table with the foot hanging free. Starting position: foot relaxed. Then slowly he moves the foot up toward the shin, pauses, slowly points it down, and returns to the starting position, while the physiotherapist watches and lightly guides the heel. Slow, controlled, comfortable range. Fixed side-on camera showing the whole lower leg and foot.

## B3 band strengthening
Same clinic, same two people. The athlete sits with the right leg extended. A light resistance band is anchored to a table leg and looped over the forefoot; he slowly turns the foot outward against the band and slowly returns it, the physiotherapist supervising next to him. Fixed camera on the lower leg.

## B4 supported balance
Same clinic, same two people. The athlete stands between parallel support rails (or holding a rail with one hand), lifts the left foot slightly and holds balance on the right foot for a few seconds, steady and controlled, the physiotherapist standing close beside. Medium shot showing his whole body.

## C1 return jog
Same athlete, on an indoor training track or turf, controlled easy jogging toward camera and past it, relaxed upright posture, physiotherapist walking along the side. Tracking shot.

## C2 direction change
Same athlete on turf with 4 flat cones: controlled, moderate-pace side-step and change of direction around cones, physiotherapist observing from the side with a tablet-free, hands-clasped posture.

## C3 clinic closing
Same clinic and same two people: the physiotherapist smiles and speaks with the athlete, reviewing his standing posture; both look relaxed and confident. Slow dolly in, then still.
